answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed on proven misbehavior, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs real capital instead of being free. Reputation then grows like a grove: each agent's record of completed work compounds slowly, and a fresh identity cannot borrow an old one's trust. A voyage of verified transactions across independent counterparties is the only path to high-value jobs, pushing the attacker's cost above any gain and keeping the horizon open to honest newcomers who earn trust gradually.
